feature: A title's size is a number you type or nudge
summary: Size in the Text section is now a box you type any size into, beside the Weight dropdown on one line, the way the title mock draws it. The preset sizes are on a small list at the end of the box. A Captions layer's Text section has the same box.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording, add a title with the Text tool, pick it.

try.do: Pick the title and look at the Text section: Size and Weight share one line, the word Size inside its box.
Click the Size box, type 30 and press Return: the title becomes 30 px.
Click the box again and press Shift and the up arrow: 40. The up arrow alone goes up by one.
Click the small chevron at the end of the box and pick 64 px from the presets.
Switch the Mac to Light and look again.
Pick two text layers of different sizes: Size reads Mixed, dimmed. Type 30, Return: both are 30. Press Cmd-Z once: both go back.
The same Mixed box in Light.

evaluate: Does Size beside Weight on one line read as clearly as the mock?
Is the small chevron at the end of the box enough to tell you the preset sizes are there?
Does the Size and Weight line starting at the panel's left edge, under the Font label rather than under the Font dropdown, look right to you?
Is the box right to show the number with no px after it, as the mock does?
rough: The app goes further than the mock: a chevron at the end of the Size box opens the preset sizes, which this task's own checklist asks for (a-title-s-size-is-a-number-you-type-or-nudge-the).
Dragging sideways on the word Size does not change the size yet; it is a click target that puts the keyboard in the box.
With Mixed showing, an arrow key does nothing until a number is typed; it does not step each layer from its own size.
